answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit tied to a unique cipher key that signs every action, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. When a new agent joins, peers check its signed history before trusting it; a single bad actor cannot echo the same false attestation across many fake accounts because each identity carries its own reputation and its stake is slashed on fraud. Ivory-tower rules alone never work — only bonded, verifiable identity with real cost stops cheap clones.
